evidence: The application installer calls page registration on each descriptor and stores the original page pointer in its installed array; it does not copy the page descriptor. Four separately identified manifests submit the selected descriptors for settings, heart rate, watchface and Mi Home. Page registration links each original descriptor into the page list and initializes bookkeeping fields. The UI-create wrapper searches the descriptor/parent chain for the function pointer at +76, calls it with page, root and navigation data, and ignores its return; the UI-destroy path similarly calls the pointer at +100 with the page and ignores its return. Each selected startup descriptor contains its analyzed creation and UI-destroy callbacks in those slots.
scope: calls reaching each particular page descriptor callback slot; page callbacks reached through a different pointer or direct calls are not intercepted
limitations: Registration and indirect dispatch are statically analyzed; live slot persistence and page lifecycle are not yet device verified. The page root is checked at install and detach but may not yet be populated while creation has started, and is not a system-wide execution barrier. Skipping or rewriting creation or destruction can break page state, leak resources or leave callbacks active. The create return is not used by the observed lifecycle caller and has no confirmed meaning. Runtime unload, raw replacements and concurrent code publication remain unprotected.
additional_evidence: Timer, alarm, weather, sleep and oxygen manifests register the same startup descriptors via the app installer. The page manager stores its newly created root at descriptor +48 before the create callback and clears that field after the UI-destroy callback; this slot and the app-specific state slot gate installation and detach. Launcher, sport list, stress and breathing manifests at 0x0c51739c, 0x0c5c34ac, 0x0c628f00 and 0x0c628fbc register the selected initial descriptors. The sport list state slot is the descriptor-owned allocation at +60; the other three slots are application globals set/cleared by their create/destroy routines.
